options.description: Same category, but the failure carries kj for AbsentAncestor and BlockedByItem. Needs a listing or stat walk on object stores to find kj: extra requests on every miss.

options.label: Three distinct categories
options.description: Mirrors KEY-013 one to one. Callers must catch three things for 'not there'; costs the same extra requests.

options.label: Backend client defaults
options.description: Profile-declared per backend; one caller's code waits 20 s on one backend and forever on another.

questions.question: AX-6, the Closed state. Scenario: the caller leaves a `with` block, then calls read(10) and close() again. What happens?

options.label: Python io semantics (Recommended)
options.description: read, readinto, readline and chunks raise ValueError ('I/O operation on closed file'), a caller error, not a storage category; close() again is a no-op. Same in async. Source: io.IOBase.close docs.

options.label: A library 'closed' category
options.description: Reads raise a library error. Breaks code that expects file-object behaviour (wrappers check ValueError), with no gain: nothing about the store happened.

questions.question: AX-6, the Failed state. Scenario: a stream read surfaces a transport failure that the library's own recovery (AX-13) could not mend; the caller catches it and calls read(10) again. What happens?

options.label: Sticky: same failure again (Recommended)
options.description: Every later read raises the same category; close() works and releases. The caller never gets bytes after a gap. Recovery is the library's job inside a read (AX-13), so a caller retry means a new OP-01 call. Source: Go bufio.Reader's sticky error.

options.label: Later reads try again
options.description: The next read attempts to resume from the position. Two places that resume (inside a read and across reads), each needing its own pinning rule.

options.label: Stream becomes Closed
options.description: Later reads raise ValueError as if closed; the original failure is lost to code that reads on.

questions.question: AX-6, an unclosed stream. Scenario: the caller drops the last reference to an open stream without close(). What is promised?

options.label: Released when collected, ResourceWarning (Recommended)
options.description: Its connection or file descriptor is released when the object is collected, with a ResourceWarning; when that happens is not promised (AX-14). Source: CPython file objects.

options.label: Released, no warning
options.description: Silent: leaked streams in long-running code go unnoticed until the pool runs dry.

questions.question: AX-6, the handle's lifetime ends while a stream is open (shared.md § Lifetime: 'OP-21's flow adds how a lifetime ends'). Scenario: open stream, handle closed, then stream.read(10).

options.label: Leave to OP-21, open item (Recommended)
options.description: The cell stays explicitly open, blocked on OP-21's session, which decides how a lifetime ends for every handed-out resource at once. Source: shared.md § Lifetime.

options.label: Decide now: stream outlives it
options.description: A stream keeps working until its own close; OP-21 must then keep the connection alive for open streams. object_store streams hold the client this way.

options.label: Decide now: stream fails
options.description: The next read raises a 'closed' failure; OP-21 must invalidate every stream it handed out. gocloud Bucket.Close's model.

questions.question: AX-11, opening a stream. Scenario: open a stream on 'missing' or on folder 'd'. When does not-found or not-an-item surface?

options.label: At the open call, always (Recommended)
options.description: The open classifies (D22's t0), so key refused, not found, not an item, permission, authentication and not readable surface from the open itself; a stream the caller holds is for an item that existed. Costs the first request at open. Source: session input pitfall 'pyarrow's allow_delayed_open defers open errors to close'; Python open().

options.label: At the first read
options.description: Open is free and lazy; every caller must expect not-found from read(), and an unread stream never learns the key was missing.

questions.question: AX-11, closing a stream. Scenario: a stream meets E8 while releasing its connection in close(). May close() raise a storage failure?

options.label: Never (Recommended)
options.description: Releasing a read resource has nothing to report: every byte delivered was already checked, and a failure while releasing is swallowed (logged). close() raises nothing but a cancellation (E14). Source: Python read-only file objects; fsspec read-mode close.

options.label: May raise unavailable
options.description: Callers in a `with` block then see a release failure replace the body's exception, or a successful read reported as failed.

questions.question: AX-11, a handle's start (shared.md § Lifetime: 'the span from the moment a caller holds it'). Scenario: a caller creates a store for an S3 bucket while offline, then reads. When does unavailable surface?

options.label: At the first call, never at creation (Recommended)
options.description: Creating a handle contacts no backend; a handle is usable from the moment the caller holds it, and the first operation meets E7 like any other. Reachability is OP-24's. Source: boto3 client and object_store builders (lazy connection); gocloud OpenBucket.

options.label: Creation connects
options.description: A handle that exists is known reachable at creation, but creation fails offline and every config check needs network.

questions.question: AX-13, the library's own retries (shared: 'Retry coupled to idempotency', each entry's AX-13). Scenario: a whole read meets E10 (S3 503 SlowDown) twice, then succeeds. A read changes nothing (D10), so repeating it is safe. What does the library do?

options.label: Built-in, bounded, configurable (Recommended)
options.description: Transient failures (E7, E8, E9, E10, E12) are retried with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After, up to a per-store attempt limit, default 3 attempts per backend request; only then does unavailable/timeout surface. Never retries not found, access, not readable, changed. Source: session input Q4 Retries (object_store built in, idempotent only; s3fs allow-list); botocore standard mode, 3 attempts.

options.label: No library retries
options.description: Every transient failure surfaces at once; each caller writes its own loop. OpenDAL's default (opt-in layer).

options.label: Backend client defaults
options.description: Whatever botocore, azure-core, paramiko do; a profile row, with differing attempt counts and retryable sets per backend.

questions.question: AX-13, resuming a stream. Scenario: after 30 GB of a 40 GB stream, E8 resets the connection. What happens inside the next read?

options.label: Resume pinned, else fail (Recommended)
options.description: The library re-requests from the current position, conditioned on the content pinned at open (ETag/generation/version, an SFTP handle still open); the read continues seamlessly or, if the pin no longer holds, fails 'changed' (D22). Where a backend cannot pin a new request, it fails unavailable: a variation point (AX-15). Each resume has the attempt budget afresh once bytes have flowed. Source: s3fs ETag-checked range refetch (session input).

options.description: Any mid-stream drop fails the stream; a 40 GB read must restart from 0, and long streams fail in proportion to their length.

questions.question: AX-13, the library's own retries (shared: 'Retry coupled to idempotency', each entry's AX-13). Scenario: a whole read meets E10 (S3 503 SlowDown) twice, then succeeds. A read changes nothing (D10), so repeating it is safe. What does the library do?

options.description: The library re-requests from the current position, conditioned on the content pinned at open (ETag/generation/version, an SFTP handle still open); the read continues seamlessly or, if the pin no longer holds, fails 'changed' (D22). Where a backend cannot pin a new request, it fails unavailable: a variation point (AX-15). Each resume has the attempt budget afresh once bytes have flowed. Source: s3fs ETag-checked range refetch (session input).
options.label: Resume pinned, else fail (Recommended)

options.description: Any mid-stream drop fails the stream; a 40 GB read must restart from 0, and long streams fail in proportion to their length.
options.label: Never resume a stream

AX-14, the stream's memory (N-02: 'without holding it in memory'). Scenario: a 40 GB stream read in 1 MiB pieces. cloudpathlib downloads the whole object first (session input pitfall). Is a bound promised?

options.label: Promise: bounded, no whole copy (Recommended)
options.description: A stream holds at most a per-store buffer bound independent of the item's size, plus what the caller's own read(n) or chunk size asks for, and never stages the item in memory or on local disk. The buffer's exact size and read-ahead are not promised. Source: catalogue N-02; session input pitfall 'cloudpathlib downloads the whole object first'.

options.label: Not promised
options.description: A backend may stage to a temp file; N-02 holds only in spirit, and disk fills on large reads.

AX-15, pinned resume on SFTP (D39). Scenario: an SFTP stream's connection drops at 30 GB; the open file handle is gone, and a reopened handle cannot prove it is the same file (SFTP has no ETag; S3, Azure and GCS pin by ETag/generation, Local's descriptor never drops). What does SFTP declare?

options.label: Deviation: no resume, fails unavailable (Recommended)
options.description: Honest: an SFTP stream that loses its connection is Failed; the caller restarts. Normal value stays 'resume pinned'. Source: SFTP v3 (draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02) has no content identity.

options.label: Resume when size and mtime match
options.description: Usually right, but not a pin (mtime granularity, preserved mtime): it would let D22's 'never another content' fail silently.

questions.question: AX-15, static or probed. Scenario: an S3 backend pointed at a non-AWS S3-compatible endpoint whose consistency and If-Match support are unknown. How is a store's variation fixed?

options.label: Static; config selects, weaker by default (Recommended)
options.description: Each backend declares its variation statically; where one backend serves services that differ (S3-compatible endpoints), the store's configuration selects the declaration, and an unnamed non-AWS endpoint gets the deviations (eventual, no pinned resume). No probing. Source: unsourced.

options.label: Static, normal values for every S3 endpoint
options.description: Simplest; an endpoint that is not strongly consistent then breaks D23 undeclared.

options.label: Probed at first use
options.description: The library tests the endpoint (e.g. a conditional GET); costs requests and needs write access to test consistency.

questions.question: AX-15, a caller who needs the stronger guarantee. Scenario: a caller's correctness rests on read-after-write (D23) or pinned resume (D39). Can it request it?

options.label: No request in OP-01; learn via OP-18 (Recommended)
options.description: OP-01 takes no 'require' option; a caller checks the store's profile through OP-18 (shared.md: 'How a caller learns a store's profile: OP-18's flow') and refuses for itself. Keeps OP-01's signature free of policy.

options.label: A per-call 'require' option
options.description: OP-01 fails fast with an unsupported category when the store's declaration is weaker. Every entry would then need the same option for consistency.
